hazards.hazard: TBC (tert-butylcatechol) injection failure at V-104 outlet — butadiene polymerizes exothermically in the 400 m insulated rundown line and storage spheres, plugging the line, building pressure, and rupturing equipment with massive flammable release
hazards.reason: Butadiene inventory in the 400 m line and spheres is large; polymerization is rapid once inhibitor drops below ~50 ppm. Package notes only continuous injection at 50–100 ppm with no backup pump, no TBC flow alarm, no rundown temperature monitoring, and no quench system. Consequence is catastrophic;,

hazards.hazard: Trace acetylenes in crude C4 feed meet copper/brass instrument fittings or tubing — form shock-sensitive copper acetylide that detonates from vibration or thermal shock
hazards.reason: Feed explicitly contains traces of acetylenes. Copper/brass is common in instrument taps, gauge roots, and analyzer lines — none of which are called out as prohibited. No acetylene-specific safeguard (e.g., acetylenic guard bed, copper-free specs) is mentioned. Detonation can initiate a larger butad

hazards.hazard: Low-pressure steam supply to C-104 reboiler E-104 loses pressure control (regulator fails open or control valve sticks) — column overheats, butadiene vapor pressure exceeds 5 bar g design, relief lifts to flare
hazards.reason: C-104 operates at ~5 bar g with a low-pressure steam reboiler; a steam-side overpressure is a classic cause. Safeguards listed: high-pressure alarm on columns and relief valves to flare — but only a basic control system, no SIS, no steam pressure trip. Flare capacity for simultaneous multi-relief

hazards.hazard: P-104A seal failure or deadheading during changeover to spare P-104B (block valves misoperated) — large butadiene release at pump area, ignition from hot surfaces or static
hazards.reason: Changeover occurs a few times per year; spare suction/discharge block valves are normally closed — misoperation sequence (open suction before discharge, or vice versa) can deadhead the running pump or start the spare against closed discharge. Hydrocarbon detectors only at pump area and column base;

hazards.hazard: Fire or common-cause overpressure lifts multiple relief valves simultaneously — flare header/knockout drum overwhelmed, flare tip extinguishes, hydrocarbon discharges at grade forming vapor cloud explosion
equipment: relief valves (all columns, drums, pump discharge)
hazards.reason: All relief valves discharge to a single flare header. Package gives no flare capacity, knockout drum sizing, purge gas backup, or flame-front monitoring. A unit fire (credible from butadiene leak) would challenge all reliefs at once. Residential area 1 km away — off-site consequence severe.

hazards.hazard: Flow stops in rundown line (pump trip, start-up, shutdown) — stagnant butadiene polymerizes even with residual TBC, plugs 400 m insulated line; restart attempts overpressure and rupture line
hazards.reason: Line is long, insulated, and holds large butadiene volume. Bypass around E-106 and start-up recycle line are normally closed; recycle last used 14 months ago — likely corroded/blocked. No line temperature or flow-loss alarm mentioned. Polymerization in stagnant lines is a known butadiene hazard.

hazards.hazard: N-methylpyrrolidone solvent lost from C-101/C-102 (leak, degradation, foam carryover) — butadiene breaks through to raffinate pipeline and heavies, creating off-spec product and downstream reactivity hazards
hazards.reason: Extractive distillation depends entirely on solvent selectivity. Antifoam injection to C-101 is the only mentioned safeguard against foam-induced solvent loss. No solvent makeup rate monitor, no raffinate butadiene analyzer, no solvent degradation tracking. Downstream units not described but raff

hazards.hazard: C-103 solvent stripper bottoms overheat (~150 °C) from reboiler control failure or fouling — solvent degrades to reactive by-products, pressure rises, toxic/flammable release via relief
hazards.reason: Stripper runs at ~150 °C bottoms — near solvent thermal degradation temperature. Only safeguards listed: high-pressure alarm on columns and relief to flare. No high-temperature trip, no reboiler steam pressure control description, no solvent quality monitoring. Degradation products can be peroxides

hazards.hazard: Hydrocarbon leak at locations without gas detectors (V-101, C-101/102, C-103, C-104, V-104 sample points, rundown line flanges, sphere vents) — vapor cloud forms undetected, delayed ignition causes flash fire or VCE
equipment: hydrocarbon gas detectors (pump area, column base only)
hazards.reason: Package explicitly lists detectors only at pump area and column base. Many potential leak points (sample connections, flanges, relief valve outlets, sphere vents) have no fixed detection. Basic control system implies no automated isolation on gas detection. Site boundary 300 m — off-site impact

hazards.reason: Line is normally closed, last used 14 months ago — valve may not seat, position indication not mentioned, no interlock with pump run status.
